question: Who was the father of Samuel from Ramathaim-zophim of Mount Ephraim, and who were his two wives?
opt1: Elkanah, an Ephrathite; and the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah
opt2: Jesse, a Bethlehemite; and his wives were Abigail and Zeruiah
opt3: Manoah, a Danite; and his wives were Deborah and Jael
opt4: Kish, a Benjamite; and his wives were Ahinoam and Rizpah
correct: Elkanah, an Ephrathite; and the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah
explanation: Elkanah was a devout Levite residing in Ramathaim-zophim; his domestic life was marked by the sorrow of bigamy, with beloved Hannah barren while Peninnah bore children. 1 Samuel 1:1-2 (KJV) - "Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah ... And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children."

question: At which spiritual center did Elkanah go up yearly to worship and sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts?
opt1: Unto Bethel, where the sacred ark of God was guarded by the elders
opt2: Unto Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were
opt3: Unto Gilgal, where the twelve memorial stones were pitched by the Jordan
opt4: Unto Jerusalem, where the royal altar of burnt offering stood upon Mount Moriah
correct: Unto Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were
explanation: Shiloh was the central sanctuary where the Tabernacle and Ark of the Covenant rested, though its priesthood was compromised by Eli's corrupt sons. 1 Samuel 1:3 (KJV) - "And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there."

question: How did Peninnah relentlessly torment and provoke Hannah year after year during the pilgrimage to Shiloh?
opt1: She demanded that Hannah pay fifty shekels of silver for the sacrificial meals
opt2: She forbade Hannah from entering into the court of the tabernacle of the congregation
opt3: Her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb
opt4: She reported Hannah to the high priest Eli as a rebellious and unholy woman
correct: Her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb
explanation: Peninnah acted as a cruel domestic adversary, weaponizing Hannah's barrenness to grieve her heart and drive her to weeping and fasting. 1 Samuel 1:6-7 (KJV) - "And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb. And as he did so year by year, when she went up to the house of the LORD, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and did not eat."

question: What loving comfort did Elkanah speak to console Hannah in her deep sorrow?
opt1: Weep no more, for tomorrow the high priest shall offer a special kid on thy behalf
opt2: Tarry at home in Ramah and journey no more unto the annual feast at Shiloh
opt3: Accept forty talents of silver and anoint thy head with precious ointment of spikenard
opt4: Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?
correct: Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?
explanation: Elkanah expressed deep marital devotion, assuring Hannah that his steadfast covenant love for her exceeded the societal prestige of ten sons. 1 Samuel 1:8 (KJV) - "Then said Elkanah her husband to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?"

question: What solemn vow did Hannah make before the LORD in the bitterness of her soul at Shiloh?
opt1: If thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid... and wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head
opt2: I will offer one hundred young bullocks upon the altar of burnt offering in Shiloh
opt3: I will fast forty days and forty nights without tasting barley bread or water
opt4: I will dedicate half of all my husband's inheritance unto the treasury of the priests
correct: If thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid... and wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head
explanation: Hannah did not merely pray for a child to end her personal reproach; she dedicated him to a lifelong Nazarite consecration to serve God in national spiritual revival. 1 Samuel 1:11 (KJV) - "And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head."

question: Why did the aged high priest Eli mistakenly rebuked Hannah as she prayed in the temple?
opt1: Because she wore garments of sackcloth within the holy court of the sanctuary
opt2: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken
opt3: Because she refused to present the required portions of meat unto Hophni and Phinehas
opt4: Because she bowed her face toward the earth during the time of the evening sacrifice
correct: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken
explanation: Eli, spiritually insensitive after years of tolerating corruption, misinterpreted Hannah's silent, anguished heart-cry as drunkenness. 1 Samuel 1:12-14 (KJV) - "Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken. And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee."

question: How did Hannah answer Eli's false accusation of drunkenness?
opt1: The curse of the daughter of Belial resteth upon the priests of this sanctuary
opt2: I have brought three talents of silver to redeem the family vows of my husband
opt3: No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD
opt4: I have fasted seven days according to the commandment of the elders of Mount Ephraim
correct: No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD
explanation: Hannah answered with profound humility and dignity, explaining that her silent agony was the pouring out of her soul before God. 1 Samuel 1:15-16 (KJV) - "And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD. Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto."

question: What benediction of faith did Eli speak that transformed Hannah's countenance?
opt1: Bring forty measures of fine flour and two turtle doves on the morrow
opt2: The high priest hath annulled thy vows before the altar of incense
opt3: May the elders of Ramah appoint thy husband as a judge over the northern tribes
opt4: Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him
correct: Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him
explanation: Eli's pastoral blessing imparted peace to Hannah's spirit; believing God's promise, she ate and her countenance was no longer sad. 1 Samuel 1:17-18 (KJV) - "Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad."

question: What name did Hannah give unto her newborn son, and what was its sacred meaning?
opt1: Called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD
opt2: Called his name Samson, saying, He shall begin to deliver Israel from oppression
opt3: Called his name Solomon, saying, The peace of God shall rest upon our family
opt4: Called his name Saul, saying, He is the choice servant of the tribe of Benjamin
correct: Called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD
explanation: 'Samuel' (Shemuel, meaning 'Heard of God' or 'Asked of God') stood as a perpetual memorial that God answers the fervent prayers of His humble servants. 1 Samuel 1:20 (KJV) - "Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD."

question: When did Hannah bring young Samuel to Shiloh to present him permanently unto the LORD?
opt1: When he reached the age of thirty years according to the law of the priests
opt2: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her... and brought the child to Eli... and she said, As long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD
opt3: Immediately on the eighth day following his circumcision according to Moses
opt4: When he was twelve years old to observe the annual feast of the Passover
correct: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her... and brought the child to Eli... and she said, As long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD
explanation: As soon as Samuel was weaned (approx. 3 years old), Hannah fulfilled her sacred vow, bringing him with sacrifices to Shiloh to serve God perpetually. 1 Samuel 1:24, 28 (KJV) - "And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her ... and brought the child to Eli ... Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD. And he worshipped the LORD there."

question: What magnificent prophetic theme opens Hannah's triumphal prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1-2?
opt1: The kings of the earth have conspired against Mount Zion, yet God shall scatter them
opt2: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD... There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God
opt3: Blessed be the high priest Eli who hath blessed my household with fruitful vineyards
opt4: The twelve tribes shall march across the river Jordan with thirty thousand chariots
correct: My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD... There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God
explanation: Hannah's song is a profound theological masterpiece and messianic archetype (directly anticipating Mary's Magnificat in Luke 1:46-55), exalting God's supreme holiness and sovereignty. 1 Samuel 2:1-2 (KJV) - "And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God."

question: How does Hannah's prayer describe God's sovereign reversal of human fortunes in 1 Samuel 2:6-7?
opt1: Earthly kings establish wealth through military conquests and taxes of silver
opt2: Man determineth his own destiny through wisdom and the strength of his right arm
opt3: The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up
opt4: The stars in their courses govern the rise and fall of the families of Israel
correct: The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up
explanation: Hannah proclaimed absolute divine supremacy over life, death, poverty, and exaltation: God humbles the arrogant and lifts the destitute from the dust. 1 Samuel 2:6-8 (KJV) - "The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD's, and he hath set the world upon them."

question: What is the first biblical occurrence of the title 'his anointed' (Messiah / Christ) in personal prayer found in 1 Samuel 2:10?
opt1: The LORD shall send Moses from heaven to restore the two tables of the law
opt2: The high priest of Shiloh shall wear the golden crown of righteousness forever
opt3: The princes of Judah shall build an imperial palace upon the heights of Carmel
opt4: The LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed
correct: The LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed
explanation: This is the very first time in Scripture that 'Messiah' ('His anointed' - Mashiach) is used in connection with a coming Davidic/eschatological King. 1 Samuel 2:10 (KJV) - "The adversaries of the LORD shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed."

question: How did Scripture describe the spiritual character and apostasy of Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas?
opt1: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD
opt2: They were faithful scribes who transcribed the law of Moses daily
opt3: They were mighty men of valour who defended the ark against the Philistines
opt4: They were holy Nazarites who abstained from all wine and strong drink
correct: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD
explanation: Despite holding the sacred office of priesthood, Hophni and Phinehas were described as 'sons of Belial' (worthless, wicked men) who were spiritually unregenerate and knew not God. 1 Samuel 2:12 (KJV) - "Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD."

question: What sacrilegious abuse did Eli's sons commit regarding the sacrificial offerings brought by worshippers?
opt1: They sold the holy incense of the sanctuary to Canaanite merchants for gold
opt2: The priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand... All that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself... before they burnt the fat
opt3: They offered unclean swine upon the altar of burnt offering in the court
opt4: They poured the consecrated wine into the river Jordan before the new moon
correct: The priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand... All that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself... before they burnt the fat
explanation: They committed violent extortion: demanding raw meat before God's portion (the fat) was burned on the altar, showing contempt for God's holy sacrifices. 1 Samuel 2:13-17 (KJV) - "And the priests' custom with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand; And he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither. Also before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw. And if any man said unto him, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would answer him, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD: for men abhorred the offering of the LORD."

question: What loving annual gift did Hannah bring to young Samuel whenever she and Elkanah came to Shiloh?
opt1: A pair of golden sandals embroidered with blue linen threads
opt2: A silver horn filled with fragrant anointing oil from Bethlehem
opt3: His mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice
opt4: A scroll of the book of Genesis inscribed on sheepskin parchment

explanation: Hannah expressed enduring motherly tenderness: every year as Samuel grew, she lovingly crafted a new linen robe ('little coat') suited to his priestly service. 1 Samuel 2:19 (KJV) - "Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice."

question: How many additional children did the LORD graciously grant unto Hannah after she dedicated Samuel?
opt1: Seven sons, fulfilling her prophetic song of praise
opt2: Two sons and four daughters who married princes of Judah
opt3: No more children, for she had taken a lifelong vow of celibacy
opt4: Three sons and two daughters: and the child Samuel grew before the LORD

explanation: God rewarded Hannah's selfless dedication fivefold, blessing her with three more sons and two daughters while Samuel flourished in the sanctuary. 1 Samuel 2:21 (KJV) - "And the LORD visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the LORD."

question: What gross moral scandal did Eli hear that his sons were committing at the door of the tabernacle?
opt1: How they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
opt2: How they stole forty talents of refined silver from the altar treasury
opt3: How they forged bronze idols of Baal inside the holy place
opt4: How they drank wine with the ambassadors of the Philistines at night

explanation: Eli's sons turned the sacred sanctuary into a place of pagan temple prostitution, defiling women who served at the entrance of the Tabernacle. 1 Samuel 2:22 (KJV) - "Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel; and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation."

question: What profound spiritual principle did the unnamed man of God proclaim in rebuking Eli for honoring his sons above God?
opt1: The sins of the fathers shall be visited upon the third and fourth generation only
opt2: Them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed

opt4: A soft answer turneth away wrath, but grievous words stir up anger

explanation: An eternal spiritual law: God honors those who prioritize His glory, but those who treat Him with contempt will be stripped of influence and brought low. 1 Samuel 2:30 (KJV) - "... for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed."

question: What immediate sign was prophesied concerning Hophni and Phinehas to confirm the impending judgment upon Eli's house?
opt1: They shall be struck with incurable leprosy in their right hands

opt4: They shall be blinded like Samson in the prison house of Gaza

explanation: God decreed the abrupt, simultaneous death of both corrupt priests on a single battlefield day as divine proof of total judgment. 1 Samuel 2:34 (KJV) - "And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas; in one day they shall die both of them."

question: How did 1 Samuel 3:1 describe the spiritual condition of Israel regarding divine revelation in the days of young Samuel?

opt3: And the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision

correct: And the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision
explanation: 'Precious' here means rare and scarce: due to widespread priestly corruption and national compromise, direct prophetic revelation from God had virtually ceased. 1 Samuel 3:1 (KJV) - "And the child Samuel ministered unto the LORD before Eli. And the word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision."

question: Where was young Samuel lying down when the voice of the LORD first called him?
opt1: In the private tent of his father Elkanah in the camp of Ramah
opt2: In the outer court beside the altar of burnt offering at the gate
opt3: On the mountain peak of Gerizim overlooking the valley of Shechem
opt4: In the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and ere the lamp of God went out

explanation: Samuel slept in the Tabernacle precincts near the Ark, tending the sacred seven-branched golden menorah before its oil burned out at dawn. 1 Samuel 3:3 (KJV) - "And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep;"

question: How many times did the LORD call Samuel before the aged priest Eli understood that the LORD had called the child?
opt1: Three times Samuel ran unto Eli; and Eli perceived the third time that the LORD had called the child
opt2: Seven times, corresponding to the seven lamps of the golden candlestick
opt3: Two times, after which Samuel went out to the gate of Shiloh
opt4: Five times, while Eli was offering the morning incense on the altar
correct: Three times Samuel ran unto Eli; and Eli perceived the third time that the LORD had called the child
explanation: Not yet recognizing God's voice, Samuel ran dutifully to Eli three consecutive times, until Eli finally perceived that God was speaking to the boy. 1 Samuel 3:4-8 (KJV) - "That the LORD called Samuel: and he answered, Here am I. And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down. And the LORD called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again. Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, neither was the word of the LORD yet revealed unto him. And the LORD called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the LORD had called the child."

question: What respectful words of submission did Eli instruct Samuel to speak if the voice called him again?
opt1: Here am I, Lord; command thy prophet what to do
opt2: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
opt3: Arise, O God, and deliver thy people from the Philistines
opt4: Reveal thy secret name, O God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
correct: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth
explanation: Eli taught Samuel the quintessential posture of humble, attentive discipleship: presenting himself as a listening servant ready to obey God's Word. 1 Samuel 3:9 (KJV) - "Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place."

question: How did the divine presence manifest when God called Samuel the fourth time?
opt1: A great whirlwind shook the curtains of the tabernacle with thunder
opt2: A pillar of fire descended upon the golden mercy seat of the ark
opt3: And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth

explanation: The Scripture indicates a personal theophany ('the LORD came, and stood'), repeating his name with intimate urgency: 'Samuel, Samuel!' 1 Samuel 3:10 (KJV) - "And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth."

question: What terrifying message of judgment did the LORD reveal to young Samuel concerning the house of Eli?
opt1: Eli shall be struck with blindness and wander as an exile in Moab
opt2: The tabernacle of Shiloh shall be transported to the territory of Dan
opt3: Hophni and Phinehas shall repent and be restored after forty days
opt4: I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken... because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not
correct: I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken... because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not
explanation: Eli's fatal failure was passive parenting and compromised leadership: knowing his sons committed vile sacrilege, he failed to restrain or depose them from the priesthood. 1 Samuel 3:11-13 (KJV) - "And the LORD said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not."

question: Why could the iniquity of Eli's house never be purged with sacrifice nor offering forever?
opt1: Because they had willfully despised and blasphemed God's holy sacrifices with high-handed rebellion and unrepentant contempt

opt3: Because the high priest had forgotten to recite the name of God on the Day of Atonement
opt4: Because the altar of burnt offering had been broken by Philistine raiders
correct: Because they had willfully despised and blasphemed God's holy sacrifices with high-handed rebellion and unrepentant contempt
explanation: When the sacrificial system itself is intentionally corrupted and mocked by the priests, no ritual animal sacrifice can substitute for heartfelt repentance. 1 Samuel 3:14 (KJV) - "And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever."

question: How did Eli respond when young Samuel faithfully recounted the entire terrifying vision of judgment without hiding anything?
opt1: He rent his clothes and commanded forty days of national fasting at Shiloh
opt2: It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good

question: What statement in 1 Samuel 3:19 verified that God authenticated every prophetic word spoken by Samuel?
opt1: And Samuel was crowned king over the twelve united tribes of Israel

question: How widely was Samuel recognized and established as a prophet of the LORD throughout the land?
opt1: Only within his home tribe of Ephraim and the family of Elkanah
opt2: Among the seventy elders of Shiloh who guarded the golden candlestick

question: Where did Israel encamp against the Philistines, and how many Israelites fell in the first military engagement?
opt1: Encamped at the valley of Elah; and twenty-two thousand Israelites fell

explanation: Israel suffered an initial defeat of 4,000 men at Ebenezer near Aphek, shaking their military confidence. 1 Samuel 4:1-2 (KJV) - "And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and pitched beside Ebenezer: and the Philistines pitched in Aphek. And the Philistines put themselves in array against Israel: and when they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines: and they slew of the army in the field about four thousand men."

question: What superstitious decision did the elders of Israel make to try to secure victory after their initial defeat?
opt1: Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of Shiloh unto us, that, when it cometh among us, it may save us out of the hand of our enemies
opt2: Let us humble ourselves in sackcloth and ashes for forty days of repentance
opt3: Let us hire forty thousand mercenary archers from the princes of Egypt
opt4: Let us send ambassadors to sign a peace treaty with the five lords of Gaza

question: What dramatic supernatural event constituted the third sign at Gibeah-elohim (the hill of God)?
opt1: Meeting a company of prophets with psaltery, tabret, pipe, and harp; the Spirit of the LORD coming upon Saul, turning him into another man
opt2: A pillar of cloud descending upon Saul's tent, while fire consumed his evening sacrifice
opt3: A sword falling from heaven into Saul's hand while the Philistine garrison fled in terror
opt4: Hearing the voice of an archangel speaking from the branches of a burning pomegranate tree
correct: Meeting a company of prophets with psaltery, tabret, pipe, and harp; the Spirit of the LORD coming upon Saul, turning him into another man
explanation: Saul experienced ecstatic prophetic empowerment as the Holy Spirit dramatically transformed his inner disposition for royal leadership. 1 Samuel 10:5-6 (KJV) - "After that thou shalt come to the hill of God, where is the garrison of the Philistines ... thou shalt meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a tabret, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they shall prophesy: And the Spirit of the LORD will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man."

question: What crucial operational instruction did Samuel give Saul concerning his appointment at Gilgal?
opt1: "Three days shalt thou fast, and on the fourth day lead Israel against Ammon"
opt2: "Seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do"
opt3: "Tarry at the fortress until the high priest brings the Urim and Thummim from Shiloh"
opt4: "Blow the trumpet throughout Benjamin, and do not fight until Samuel anoints Jonathan"
correct: "Seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do"
explanation: This specific command to wait seven days at Gilgal established the divine test of obedience that Saul would tragically fail in chapter 13. 1 Samuel 10:8 (KJV) - "And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do."

question: What famous national proverb arose when the inhabitants of the land saw Saul prophesying among the sons of the prophets?
opt1: "Can any good thing come out of Benjamin?"
opt2: "A king in appearance, but a seer in tongue!"
opt3: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
opt4: "Behold, the tall pine among the reeds of the Jordan!"
correct: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
explanation: The unexpected spiritual ecstasy of a wealthy, secular young farmer inspired an enduring proverb highlighting dramatic spiritual transformation. 1 Samuel 10:11-12 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"

question: When Saul returned home and his uncle questioned him about his discourse with Samuel, what critical detail did Saul withhold?
opt1: The location of the lost asses of Kish
opt2: The gift of the quarter-shekel of silver given by the servant
opt3: The prophecy concerning the famine in Benjamin
opt4: The matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake
correct: The matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake
explanation: Exercising prudent discretion and modesty prior to public manifestation, Saul divulged only that the asses were found, concealing his royal destiny. 1 Samuel 10:16 (KJV) - "And Saul said unto his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not."

question: At the national assembly at Mizpeh, through what divine process was Saul publicly singled out before all the tribes of Israel?
opt1: By sacred lot: first the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and finally Saul the son of Kish
opt2: By a popular democratic vote conducted among all the elders and captains of thousands
opt3: By Saul stepping forward and lifting the ark of the covenant onto his broad shoulders
opt4: By the appearance of a miraculous column of fire hovering directly over the house of Kish
correct: By sacred lot: first the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and finally Saul the son of Kish
explanation: God confirmed His private choice of Saul through the sacred lot, moving systematically from tribe to clan to the individual. 1 Samuel 10:20-21 (KJV) - "And when Samuel had caused all the tribes of Israel to come near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken. When he had caused the tribe of Benjamin to come near by their families, the family of Matri was taken, and Saul the son of Kish was taken ..."

question: Where was Saul discovered hiding when the people inquired of the LORD because they could not locate him?
opt1: In the secret chamber behind the holy altar of incense
opt2: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff" (the baggage and camp supplies)
opt3: In a subterranean cave on the outskirts of Mizpeh
opt4: Under the chariot of the prince of the tribe of Judah
correct: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff" (the baggage and camp supplies)
explanation: Overcome by modesty or intimidation at the immense weight of the office, Saul hid himself among the travelers' baggage. 1 Samuel 10:22 (KJV) - "Therefore they enquired of the LORD further, if the man should yet come thither. And the LORD answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff."

question: How did Saul react when certain 'children of Belial' (worthless men) despised him, saying, 'How shall this man save us?' and brought him no presents?
opt1: Saul ordered his bodyguard to bind them and cast them into prison
opt2: Saul called down a curse of leprosy upon their households and cattle
opt3: Saul 'held his peace' (showed restraint and remained silent)
opt4: Saul stripped them of their tribal inheritance and banished them to Moab
correct: Saul 'held his peace' (showed restraint and remained silent)
explanation: Saul demonstrated remarkable initial magnanimity, patient self-control, and wisdom by refusing to retaliate against his detractors. 1 Samuel 10:27 (KJV) - "But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he held his peace."

question: Which brutal Ammonite monarch besieged Jabesh-gilead, and what savage condition of surrender did he dictate?
opt1: Hanun the Ammonite; demanding that all their youth be sent into perpetual slavery in Rabbah
opt2: Hadadezer of Zobah; demanding all the gold shields and sacred vessels of the sanctuary
opt3: Nahash the Ammonite; demanding that he might thrust out all their right eyes for a reproach upon all Israel
opt4: Eglon of Moab; demanding an annual tribute of ten thousand fat lambs and rams
correct: Nahash the Ammonite; demanding that he might thrust out all their right eyes for a reproach upon all Israel
explanation: Nahash demanded the barbaric mutilation of their right eyes, which would render the men militarily ineffective in shield combat while humiliating all Israel. 1 Samuel 11:1-2 (KJV) - "Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead ... And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel."

question: How long of a respite did the desperate elders of Jabesh-gilead obtain from Nahash to seek a deliverer among the coasts of Israel?
opt1: Three days' respite
opt2: Fourteen days' respite
opt3: Thirty days' respite
opt4: Seven days' respite
correct: Seven days' respite
explanation: Confident in his military supremacy, Nahash arrogantly granted a week's truce, believing no Hebrew leader possessed the power to rescue Jabesh-gilead. 1 Samuel 11:3 (KJV) - "And the elders of Jabesh said unto him, Give us seven days' respite, that we may send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel: and then, if there be no man to save us, we will come out to thee."

question: Where was Saul and what was he doing when the weeping messengers from Jabesh-gilead brought word to Gibeah?
opt1: He was coming after the herd out of the field, laboring as an ordinary farmer
opt2: He was sitting on his ivory throne dispensing royal decrees to his captains
opt3: He was training chosen archers in the valley of Rephaim
opt4: He was celebrating the feast of trumpets at the sanctuary of Gilgal
correct: He was coming after the herd out of the field, laboring as an ordinary farmer
explanation: Despite his public selection at Mizpeh, Saul had quietly returned to his family farm in Gibeah, plowing behind his herd. 1 Samuel 11:5 (KJV) - "And, behold, Saul came after the herd out of the field; and Saul said, What aileth the people that they weep? And they told him the tidings of the men of Jabesh."

question: What dramatic, symbolic summons did Saul execute when the Spirit of God came mightily upon him in righteous anger?
opt1: He sounded seven silver shofars from the peak of Mount Gerizim
opt2: He hewed a yoke of oxen in pieces and sent the severed parts throughout all Israel by messengers
opt3: He set fire to the high watchtower of Geba to signal imminent invasion
opt4: He dipped a royal standard in blood and unfurled it across the Jordan valley
correct: He hewed a yoke of oxen in pieces and sent the severed parts throughout all Israel by messengers
explanation: Echoing the ancient Levite's grim summons in Judges 19, Saul cut his working oxen into pieces, mobilizing the fragmented nation under fierce leadership. 1 Samuel 11:6-7 (KJV) - "And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly. And he took a yoke of oxen, and hewed them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel by the hands of messengers ..."

question: What terrifying warning accompanied the dismembered oxen sent across the tribal territories of Israel?
opt1: "Whosoever refuseth to fight shall forfeit his family inheritance and be banished to the sea"
opt2: "Whosoever hideth in his tent shall be delivered into the hand of Nahash the Ammonite"
opt3: "Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen"
opt4: "Whosoever faileth to muster shall pay a penalty of fifty shekels of unrefined silver"
correct: "Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen"
explanation: The threat of domestic economic destruction, coupled with the fear of the LORD falling upon the people, unified the tribes as one man. 1 Samuel 11:7 (KJV) - "... saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the fear of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out with one consent."

question: At what central staging city did Saul muster the army of Israel, and what were the respective battle counts of Israel and Judah?
opt1: At Jericho; two hundred thousand of Israel, and ten thousand of Judah
opt2: At Shechem; four hundred thousand of Israel, and forty thousand of Judah
opt3: At Gilgal; one hundred thousand of Israel, and twenty thousand of Judah
opt4: At Bezek; three hundred thousand of the children of Israel, and thirty thousand men of Judah
correct: At Bezek; three hundred thousand of the children of Israel, and thirty thousand men of Judah
explanation: The massive host gathered at Bezek, strategically positioned near the Jordan crossings to mount a rapid counteroffensive against Ammon. 1 Samuel 11:8 (KJV) - "And when he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand."

question: During which watch of the night did Saul's three divisions launch their surprise assault, shattering the Ammonite host?
opt1: In the morning watch, slaying the Ammonites until the heat of the day so that no two of them were left together
opt2: In the evening watch, while the Ammonites were drinking wine in their pavilions
opt3: At midnight, utilizing torches concealed within earthen pitchers
opt4: At noonday, under the blinding glare of the sun over the mountains of Gilead
correct: In the morning watch, slaying the Ammonites until the heat of the day so that no two of them were left together
explanation: Executing a brilliant dawn ambush during the morning watch (between 2:00 AM and 6:00 AM), Saul's three coordinated columns routed Nahash's forces. 1 Samuel 11:11 (KJV) - "And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the host in the morning watch, and slew the Ammonites until the heat of the day: and it came to pass, that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them were not left together."

question: In the flush of triumphant victory, what demand did the impassioned people make to Samuel concerning Saul's former critics?
opt1: "Let us crown Saul as emperor over all the nations between Egypt and Euphrates"
opt2: "Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death"
opt3: "Strip the elders of Benjamin of their lands and bestow them upon the warriors of Judah"
opt4: "Let all who did not muster at Bezek be sold as bondmen to the Phoenicians"
correct: "Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death"
explanation: The loyalist multitude demanded the immediate execution of the dissidents who had scoffed at Saul's kingship at Mizpeh. 1 Samuel 11:12 (KJV) - "And the people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death."

question: What gracious, faith-filled declaration did Saul utter to forbid vengeance against his political detractors?
opt1: "Let them be spared only if they pay a double tribute of sheep to the royal storehouse"
opt2: "Vengeance belongeth unto the judges; wait until Samuel offers the burnt sacrifice"
opt3: "There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the LORD hath wrought salvation in Israel"
opt4: "They shall be our woodcutters and water drawers for the tabernacle at Shiloh"
correct: "There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the LORD hath wrought salvation in Israel"
explanation: At this spiritual zenith of his life, Saul attributed the triumph entirely to Jehovah and extended royal clemency to his enemies. 1 Samuel 11:13 (KJV) - "And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the LORD hath wrought salvation in Israel."

question: Where did Samuel summon all Israel to renew the kingdom, and how was Saul's coronation celebrated?
opt1: At Jerusalem, where they laid the cornerstone of a royal palace and blew trumpets
opt2: At Hebron, where the priests anointed Saul with oil from the tabernacle
opt3: At Shiloh, where the ark of the covenant was brought out before the standing army
opt4: At Gilgal, where they made Saul king before the LORD, sacrificed peace offerings, and rejoiced greatly
correct: At Gilgal, where they made Saul king before the LORD, sacrificed peace offerings, and rejoiced greatly
explanation: At ancient Gilgal, cradle of Israel's conquest, the fragmented tribes reaffirmed their covenant unity under King Saul with joyful sacred sacrifices. 1 Samuel 11:14-15 (KJV) - "Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there. And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal; and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly."

question: In his farewell address to the nation, what spotless challenge did Samuel issue concerning his lifelong financial and judicial integrity?
opt1: "Have I ever led your armies into defeat or retreated before the chariots of Sisera?"
opt2: "Did I not rebuild the walls of Shiloh and double the sacred gold of the treasury?"
opt3: "Have I withheld any prophecy or hidden the secret counsels of the Urim from the elders?"
opt4: "Whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe?"
correct: "Whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe?"
explanation: Samuel stood before the nation with an unblemished record, challenging anyone to produce a single instance of corruption or extortion during his judgeship. 1 Samuel 12:3 (KJV) - "Behold, here I am: witness against me before the LORD, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you."

question: What was the unanimous public testimony of the assembled congregation in response to Samuel's challenge?
opt1: "Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand"
opt2: "Thou hast judged righteously, yet thy sons have taken bribes in Beer-sheba"
opt3: "Thou art blameless in peace, but too old to command our hosts in battle"
opt4: "The Lord is witness that thou hast built altars in every city without fault"
correct: "Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand"
explanation: The entire nation unequivocally confirmed Samuel's absolute, pristine honesty and righteousness in public service. 1 Samuel 12:4 (KJV) - "And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand."

question: Which historic deliverers and judges did Samuel cite to demonstrate that God had always saved Israel whenever they cried out in repentance?
opt1: Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, and Samson
opt2: Jerubbaal (Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel
opt3: Barak, Tola, Jair, and Ibzan
opt4: Elon, Abdon, Eli, and Phinehas
correct: Jerubbaal (Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel
explanation: Samuel rehearsed God's covenant loyalty, showing that deliverance came not through human monarchy, but through God-raised saviors when hearts turned back to Him. 1 Samuel 12:11 (KJV) - "And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe."

question: What fundamental theological crime did Samuel expose regarding their demand for a king when Nahash of Ammon threatened them?
opt1: They refused to offer the mandatory sin offering prescribed for tribal warfare
opt2: They sought an alliance with the pharaoh of Egypt instead of relying on the tabernacle
opt3: They demanded an earthly king to reign over them, 'when the LORD your God was your king'
opt4: They failed to consult the high priest at Nob before dispatching messengers to Bezek
correct: They demanded an earthly king to reign over them, 'when the LORD your God was your king'
explanation: Samuel exposed their spiritual apostasy: their demand for an earthly ruler sprang from practical atheism, ignoring Jehovah's present, almighty kingship. 1 Samuel 12:12 (KJV) - "And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the LORD your God was your king."

question: During which agricultural season did Samuel invoke a supernatural storm to convict the people of their great wickedness?

opt3: During the olive harvest in midwinter
opt4: During the wheat harvest, when thunder and rain were virtually unknown and regarded as catastrophic to crops

explanation: Rain during the dry Palestinian wheat harvest (May-June) was an extraordinary meteorological miracle demonstrating God's sovereign wrath. 1 Samuel 12:17 (KJV) - "Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the LORD, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the LORD, in asking you a king."

question: What immediate psychological and spiritual reaction swept through the congregation when the heavens thundered and poured rain?
opt1: All the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel, confessing, 'we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king'
opt2: They fled into the wilderness, accusing Samuel of practicing sorcery against the harvest
opt3: They cast their golden ornaments into the Jordan river to appease the divine anger
opt4: They deposed Saul on the spot and pleaded with Samuel to resume sole judicial rule
correct: All the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel, confessing, 'we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king'
explanation: Terrified by the roaring thunder and unseasonable tempest, the people recognized their sin and pleaded for Samuel's intercession. 1 Samuel 12:18-19 (KJV) - "So Samuel called unto the LORD; and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel. And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the LORD thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king."

question: What magnificent covenant guarantee did Samuel articulate to reassure the trembling, penitent Israelites?
opt1: "For the tabernacle at Shiloh shall stand forever as a testimony to your children"
opt2: "For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name's sake: because it hath pleased the LORD to make you his people"
opt3: "For the blood of the paschal lamb hath turned away the destroying angel from your borders"
opt4: "For your king is taller than all adversaries and shall tread down your foes"
correct: "For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name's sake: because it hath pleased the LORD to make you his people"
explanation: Samuel grounded their national security not in their flawed fidelity, but in God's sovereign pleasure and the glory of His covenant name. 1 Samuel 12:22 (KJV) - "For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name's sake: because it hath pleased the LORD to make you his people."

question: What famous commitment of pastoral intercession and instruction did Samuel utter in 1 Samuel 12:23?
opt1: "I will build an altar of twelve unhewn stones to commemorate this covenant at Gilgal"

opt4: "I will write the history of the judges on bronze plates and deposit them in the ark"

explanation: Samuel viewed failing to pray for his people as a direct sin against Jehovah, uniting ceaseless intercession with faithful teaching of God's Word. 1 Samuel 12:23 (KJV) - "Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way."

question: What single comprehensive exhortation did Samuel give to guide Israel's future conduct before God?
opt1: "Offer twenty bullocks on every new moon and blow the trumpets across the valleys"
opt2: "Conquer the seven nations of Canaan and dismantle every iron chariot in the land"
opt3: "Pay your royal tithes promptly to the king's treasury that his throne may be established"
opt4: "Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you"

explanation: True biblical faith is characterized by heartfelt reverence and grateful service inspired by recalling God's mighty past deliverances. 1 Samuel 12:24 (KJV) - "Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you."

question: What chilling prophetic warning concluded Samuel's address if Israel persisted in rebellion against the LORD?
opt1: "But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king"
opt2: "The heavens shall become brass, the earth iron, and your cities desolate ruins"
opt3: "The Philistines shall capture the ark once more and carry it into Ashdod"
opt4: "Thy king shall be blinded and led with chains into the land of the Chaldeans"

explanation: Having an earthly king would provide zero immunity against divine judgment; persistent wickedness would destroy both ruler and subjects alike. 1 Samuel 12:25 (KJV) - "But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king."

question: How did King Saul strategically station his regular standing army of three thousand chosen men of Israel?
opt1: Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and Mount Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin
opt2: One thousand each in Gilgal, Shiloh, and Mizpeh under three captains
opt3: Two thousand with Jonathan at the Jordan crossings, and one thousand with Saul at Ramah

correct: Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and Mount Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin
explanation: Saul established a standing regular army divided between his main force at Michmash and Jonathan's contingent at Gibeah. 1 Samuel 13:2 (KJV) - "Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel; whereof two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in mount Beth-el, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent."

question: What daring military strike by Prince Jonathan provoked open war with the Philistines?
opt1: Jonathan captured the Philistine supply depot at Ashdod
opt2: Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba
opt3: Jonathan assassinated the five lords of the Philistines at Ekron
opt4: Jonathan burned thirty Philistine iron chariots in the valley of Sorek
correct: Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba
explanation: Jonathan's aggressive strike against the Philistine outpost at Geba shattered the oppressive truce and ignited all-out warfare. 1 Samuel 13:3 (KJV) - "And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear."

question: How vast was the massive Philistine retaliatory host assembled against Israel at Michmash?
opt1: Ten thousand chariots, twenty thousand horsemen, and forty thousand archers
opt2: Twelve thousand chariots, four thousand horsemen, and five hundred giant warriors
opt3: Thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude
opt4: Fifty thousand footmen, three thousand iron wagons, and ten thousand slingers

question: Where did the terrified Israelites hide themselves when they saw the colossal Philistine horde?
opt1: Behind the stone walls of Jerusalem and the fortress of Zion
opt2: In the fortified cities of Judah and the high towers of Gilead
opt3: Under the waters of the Jordan and within the reeds of the Dead Sea
opt4: In caves, in thickets, in rocks, in high places, and in pits
correct: In caves, in thickets, in rocks, in high places, and in pits
explanation: Utter panic seized the Hebrews; stripped of morale, they abandoned their villages and hid in subterranean caverns, clefts, and cisterns. 1 Samuel 13:6 (KJV) - "When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, (for the people were distressed,) then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits."

question: How long did Saul wait at Gilgal according to the set time appointed by Samuel before succumbing to panic?

opt2: Three days
opt3: Ten days
opt4: Fourteen days

explanation: Saul waited until the seventh day, but when Samuel seemed late and his soldiers began deserting en masse, his faith broke down. 1 Samuel 13:8 (KJV) - "And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him."

question: What fatal sacrilege did King Saul commit when his troops began deserting him at Gilgal?
opt1: He erected an altar to Dagon to secure peace with the Philistine lords
opt2: He intruded into the holy priestly office and offered the burnt offering and peace offerings himself
opt3: He cast lots with pagan divination arrows to determine battle strategy
opt4: He commanded that the holy ark of God be opened to inspect the two stone tablets
correct: He intruded into the holy priestly office and offered the burnt offering and peace offerings himself
explanation: Presuming upon sacred priestly prerogatives, Saul unlawfully offered sacrifices, demonstrating impatience, unbelief, and disregard for God's holy order. 1 Samuel 13:9 (KJV) - "And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering."

question: What fourfold justification did Saul offer when Samuel arrived and demanded, 'What hast thou done?'
opt1: The priests were sick, the army was starving, Jonathan was surrounded, and the sun was setting
opt2: A prophet from Bethel authorized the sacrifice, the fire fell from heaven, the Philistines fled, and Saul rejoiced
opt3: The people were scattered, Samuel came not within the days, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, and Saul 'forced' himself to supplicate the LORD
opt4: The elders urged him, the animals were dying, the altar was ready, and the ark was departing

explanation: Saul deflected guilt by blaming his scattering troops, Samuel's apparent delay, the Philistine menace, and pious rationalization ('I forced myself'). 1 Samuel 13:11-12 (KJV) - "And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash; Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal ... I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering."

question: What severe sentence did Samuel pronounce against Saul for failing to keep the commandment of the LORD?

opt2: In the wilderness of Shur
opt3: In the wilderness of Maon, on opposite sides of the mountain
opt4: In the wilderness of Kadesh

explanation: Saul and his troops were actively encircling David's mountain in Maon, cutting off all retreat. 1 Samuel 23:26 (KJV) - "And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them."

question: What sudden crisis forced Saul to abandon his pursuit at the critical moment, and what commemorative name was given to that rock?
opt1: A violent thunderstorm ignited the mountain forest; the place was named Bozez

correct: A messenger reported that the Philistines had invaded the land; the place was named Sela-hammahlekoth (The Rock of Escape / Division)
explanation: Providence orchestrated a Philistine border raid at the exact second Saul was closing the trap, prompting the renaming of the cliff as 'The Rock of Escape'. 1 Samuel 23:27-28 (KJV) - "But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come; for the Philistines have invaded the land. Wherefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth."

question: How many chosen men out of all Israel did Saul take to hunt David upon the 'rocks of the wild goats' in En-gedi?
opt1: One thousand chosen men
opt2: Six hundred chosen men
opt3: Ten thousand chosen men
opt4: Three thousand chosen men

explanation: Saul deployed an elite force of three thousand crack troops into the barren limestone precipices of En-gedi. 1 Samuel 24:2 (KJV) - "Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats."

question: For what private purpose did Saul enter the very cave where David and his men were concealed in the dark recesses?
opt1: To cover his feet (to relieve himself)

opt4: To interrogate a captured shepherd from the wilderness of Judah

explanation: Saul stepped unaccompanied into the cavern to attend to bodily needs, entirely unaware that David's men were watching from the interior shadows. 1 Samuel 24:3 (KJV) - "And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave."

explanation: David quietly crept up and sliced off the hem of Saul's royal garment as physical proof of his mercy. 1 Samuel 24:4 (KJV) - "And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee ... Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily."

question: How did David react internally immediately after cutting off the skirt of Saul's robe?
opt1: David rejoiced aloud with his men at having outsmarted the king
opt2: David was terrified that Saul's three thousand guards would enter the cave

explanation: David possessed such exquisite spiritual sensitivity that even diminishing the king's royal garment felt like an assault on God's anointed. 1 Samuel 24:5 (KJV) - "And it came to pass afterward, that David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's skirt."

question: What principle of sacred reverence did David declare to restrain his men from harming Saul?
opt1: "Let no blood be shed within this cave, for the ground is holy tabernacle ground"
opt2: "If we slay the king, the army of Benjamin will slaughter our families in Bethlehem"

explanation: David recognized that Saul's office was consecrated by God, firmly refusing to take royal authority through personal violence. 1 Samuel 24:6 (KJV) - "And he said unto his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD's anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the LORD."

explanation: David cited an ancient proverb to demonstrate that if he were truly a wicked traitor as Saul claimed, he would have committed murder when given the chance. 1 Samuel 24:13 (KJV) - "As saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but mine hand shall not be upon thee."

question: With what two humble, self-deprecating metaphors did David describe his insignificance before the King of Israel?

question: How did King Saul react when he realized David had spared his life inside the cave?
opt1: Saul commanded his archers to surround David and shoot him on the spot
opt2: Saul fell into a silent stupor and was carried back to his chariot by Abner
opt3: Saul lifted up his voice, wept, and confessed, 'Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil'
opt4: Saul demanded that David return the severed skirt of his royal robe
correct: Saul lifted up his voice, wept, and confessed, 'Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil'
explanation: Overcome by David's astonishing mercy, Saul broke down in tears, openly confessing David's superior righteousness. 1 Samuel 24:16-17 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept. And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil."

question: What certainty did Saul openly acknowledge regarding David's future and the kingdom of Israel?

explanation: Saul verbally ratified what he had long fought against: David's inevitable, divinely established ascension to the throne. 1 Samuel 24:20 (KJV) - "And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand."

question: What oath did Saul extract from David at En-gedi before departing for Gibeah?
opt1: To swear by the LORD that David would not cut off Saul's seed after him, nor destroy his name out of his father's house

opt3: To swear that David would allow Jonathan to remain supreme commander of the army
opt4: To swear that David would give all the spoil of Goliath to the sanctuary at Nob
correct: To swear by the LORD that David would not cut off Saul's seed after him, nor destroy his name out of his father's house
explanation: Saul pleaded for dynastic mercy, securing an oath that David would not exterminate his descendants upon taking the throne. 1 Samuel 24:21-22 (KJV) - "Swear now therefore unto me by the LORD, that thou wilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou wilt not destroy my name out of my father's house. And David sware unto Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men gat them up unto the hold."

question: Where did all Israel gather to lament and bury the prophet Samuel after his death?
opt1: In his house at Ramah
opt2: In the tabernacle grounds at Shiloh
opt3: In the sacred tomb of Machpelah in Hebron
opt4: On the heights of Mount Gilboa
correct: In his house at Ramah
explanation: Samuel's death marked the end of an era; the entire nation assembled in grief to bury him at his ancestral estate in Ramah. 1 Samuel 25:1 (KJV) - "And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran."

question: How does Scripture describe Nabal of Carmel and his wife Abigail regarding character and appearance?
opt1: Abigail was a wealthy heiress of Ephraim; but Nabal was a drunken priest of the line of Phinehas
opt2: Abigail was a woman of good understanding and of a beautiful countenance; but Nabal was churlish (harsh), evil in his doings, and of the house of Caleb

correct: Abigail was a woman of good understanding and of a beautiful countenance; but Nabal was churlish (harsh), evil in his doings, and of the house of Caleb
explanation: The inspired text presents a sharp antithesis between intelligent, beautiful, gracious Abigail and her crude, belligerent husband Nabal. 1 Samuel 25:3 (KJV) - "Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb."

question: How vast was Nabal's pastoral wealth, and on what festive occasion did David send ten young men to greet him peacefully?
opt1: He had ten thousand cattle and five hundred camels, and was treading the winepress in Maon

explanation: Sheep-shearing season was traditionally a time of lavish generosity, celebration, and hospitality to surrounding protectors. 1 Samuel 25:2, 4-5 (KJV) - "And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel ... And David sent out ten young men ..."

question: With what insulting, contemptuous words did Nabal rebuff David's young men when they requested provisions?

correct: "Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master... Shall I give my bread and meat to men whom I know not whence they be?"
explanation: Nabal insolently treated David as an upstart runaway slave, denying any compensation for months of armed border protection. 1 Samuel 25:10-11 (KJV) - "And Nabal answered David's servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master. Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men, whom I know not whence they be?"

question: What immediate military command did David issue to his men upon hearing Nabal's insolent reply?

explanation: Incensed by Nabal's brazen insult, David strapped on his sword and led 400 armed warriors intending to exterminate Nabal's entire male household. 1 Samuel 25:13 (KJV) - "And David said unto his men, Gird ye on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the stuff."

question: What fatal medical catastrophe struck Nabal the morning after his drunken, king-like feast when Abigail revealed what had transpired?

And it came to pass about ten days after, that the LORD smote Nabal, that he died."
